第 79 章 Six Tips for a New Manager新经理的六个技巧

Akash Bhalla / 阿卡什·巴拉

— 第 217 页 —

It's been an interesting transition moving from the role of an individual contributor to that of someone who helps look after a team of people. Here are some of the things I've learned along the way.

从独立贡献者角色转到帮照顾一个团队的人的角色是一个有趣的转变。以下是我一路上学到的一些东西。

1. Be a Zero1. 做一个零

In the book An Astronaut's Guide to Life on Earth, Chris Hadfield talks about the concept of how in any situation you can be either a "minus one," a "zero," or a "plus one." As a new manager joining a team, there will be an innate desire to try to prove yourself as immediately productive. This is often echoed as conventional wisdom because you try your hardest to be a +1 and make your presence felt. However, the reality is that most of the time you won't have enough context of a new situation to be a positive influence, and despite your best intentions you end up being a net negative. So, be a zero. Listen and understand before you try to change something.

在《宇航员地球生活指南》一书中，Chris Hadfield 谈到一个概念：在任何情况下你可以是「负一」、「零」或「正一」。作为加入团队的新经理，会有一种天生的欲望试图证明自己立刻高效。这经常被当作传统智慧呼应，因为你最努力地做 +1、让人感受到你的存在。然而现实是，大多数时候你对新情况没有足够上下文产生积极影响，尽管你好意，最终却是净负面。所以，做一个零。在你试图改变什么之前先倾听和理解。

2. Learn to Say "Yes"2. 学会说「好」

When I think back over some of the managers I've worked for, they've often carried an air of hurriedness around them, which created an invisible barrier. As time went on, I went to these types of managers less and less, and the gap between us widened. As a direct result, I've made a conscious effort to always respond with a "yes" whenever someone asks for a minute of my time. Try your best to remove any conscious or unconscious barriers that you might be creating. Caveat: This has a potential for being overwhelming, especially when it leads to uncontrollable context switching. If this is the case, replace "yes" with "yes, how about at {later that day}?"

当我回想曾为之工作的一些经理，他们经常带着一种匆忙的气场，这创造了一个无形的障碍。随着时间推移，我越来越少去找这类经理，我们之间的差距扩大。直接结果是，我有意识地努力，每当有人要我一分钟时间时总是用「好」回应。尽你最大努力消除你可能创造的任何有意识或无意识的障碍。注意：这有可能让人应接不暇，尤其是当它导致不可控的上下文切换时。如果是这种情况，把「好」换成「好，今天晚些时候怎么样？」

— 第 218 页 —

3. Learn to Say "No"3. 学会说「不」

There's a limit to how much any one person can do: trying to put more water into a full bucket isn't going to net you any more water than you already had. It's tough, but you need to learn to say "no." Understand what the most effective use of your time is, prioritize your demands and then learn to say no to those whose issues don't make the cut, and don't forget to delegate. The alternative won't magically achieve these tasks, and ultimately damages your health, your team and your reputation.

任何一个人能做的都有限：试图往满桶里加更多水不会比你已有的净得更多水。这很难，但你需要学会说「不」。理解你时间最有效的用途是什么，给你的需求排优先级，然后对那些没入选的问题学会说不，别忘了授权。另一种选择不会神奇地完成这些任务，最终损害你的健康、你的团队和你的声誉。

4. Have One-on-Ones4. 开一对一

Your most powerful tool as a manager is information; without it, you're screwed. Here's a brief set of tips for your one-on-ones:

作为经理你最强大的工具是信息；没有它你就完了。以下是你一对一的简短技巧集：

  • Schedule for at least 30 minutes every week or fortnight.每周或每两周至少安排 30 分钟。
  • Don't have anything immediately after, leave time for it to expand if needed.之后不要马上安排事，需要时留出扩展时间。
  • Don't have more than two or three in any one day; they can be mentally exhausting, and you're no use if you can't give your full attention.一天不要超过两三个；它们精神上很累，如果你不能全神贯注就没用。
  • Don't use it as status update, focus on wider questions.不要用作状态更新，聚焦更宽的问题。
  • You shouldn't be doing most of the talking.你不应该说大部分话。
  • Keep it free form, but have some basic questions and points that you bring up.保持自由形式，但带一些基本问题和要点。

5. Stay (Relatively) Technical5. 保持（相对）技术

Your technical abilities and experience are a big part of what makes you an effective engineering manager. Keeping close to the code is essential to understand the context and to have relevant conversations. If you're anything like me, it's also essential for your own sanity! However, it's also easy to fall into the trap of doing what's comfortable and familiar rather than what is actually needed. It can feel extremely satisfying and comforting making use of old skills. But there is an entire team of developers there who could do this job as good as, if not better than, you. There might be no other managers, though, and with no one else doing that part of the job, people will begin to suffer due to neglect. You've made a choice to move your career toward management, which means making a sacrifice. Even though it's essential to stay technical, this is not the same as progressing as an individual contributor or becoming a technical lead. You're there to support.

你的技术能力和经验是让你成为有效工程经理的重要部分。靠近代码对理解上下文和进行相关对话至关重要。如果你和我一样，这对你自己的精神健全也至关重要！然而，也很容易陷入做舒适熟悉的事而非实际需要的事的陷阱。用旧技能可能感觉极其满足和安慰。但那里有一整队开发者能把这件事做得和你一样好（如果不是更好的话）。但可能没有其他经理，没有别人做那部分工作，人们会因为忽视而开始受苦。你已经选择把职业转向管理，这意味着做出牺牲。虽然保持技术很重要，但这和作为独立贡献者进步或成为技术领导不一样。你在那里是为了支持。

— 第 219 页 —

6. Let Go6. 放手

One of the most important lessons to learn as a new manager is that you can't do it all, but this is a very difficult lesson to learn. If you're anything like me, the only way to learn this lesson is the hard way. It can be an extremely difficult transition, going from being a high performer and seeing immediate and tangible results of your work to being an inexperienced manager. You'll become stressed, you'll fall back into old patterns, and you'll question yourself. Don't expect to avoid this trap; instead, do the following: Accept that you'll make this mistake; Have the knowledge and awareness to try to recognize it when it happens; Work on recovering when it does. You need to change the ways in which you perceive success. Shift the focus away from your individual contributions and instead measure yourself on the health of your team and their progress as a unit.

作为新经理要学的最重要教训之一是你做不完所有事，但这是很难学的一课。如果你和我一样，学这课的唯一方式是吃苦头。从高绩效者、看到自己工作即时 tangible 的结果，转到没经验的经理，可能是极其困难的转变。你会压力大、会退回旧模式、会质疑自己。不要指望避免这个陷阱；相反，做以下事：接受你会犯这个错；有知识和意识在它发生时认出它；它发生时努力恢复。你需要改变你感知成功的方式。把焦点从你的个人贡献移开，转而用你团队的健康和他们作为一个单元的进步来衡量自己。
